identity.name: STOVE KRAFT LIMITED
identity.industry: Consumer Durables / Small Electrical Appliances & Induction Cooking

summary.oneLiner: Stove Kraft leveraged geopolitical tailwinds (Iran war, US tariff cuts) and backward integration to drive 32.4% Q4 revenue growth, with induction cooktops surging 89.4% YoY. The commencement of IKEA billing and a shift to franchise-led retail expansion position the company for sustained >15% CAGR, though near-term PAT is suppressed by forex volatility and accounting changes on lease liabilities.

one-line thesis: Stove Kraft leveraged geopolitical tailwinds (Iran war, US tariff cuts) and backward integration to drive 32.4% Q4 revenue growth, with induction cooktops surging 89.4% YoY. The commencement of IKEA billing and a shift to franchise-led retail expansion position the company for sustained >15% CAGR, though near-term PAT is suppressed by forex volatility and accounting changes on lease liabilities.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 414.5 Cr (+32.4% YoY); EBITDA: INR 39.5 Cr (+33.9% YoY), Margin 9.5% (+113 bps YoY); PAT: INR 6.1 Cr (+317.8% YoY, base effect) but margin only 1.5% due to ~INR 10-12 Cr one-off forex loss and increased interest from sale-leaseback; Order Book: Implicitly strong with induction demand exceeding 4-5 Mn unit capacity; Net Debt: Reduced via repayment, but interest charges rose to INR 25 Cr due to lease liability accounting and suppliers' credit interest.
guidance: Revenue Growth: >15% for FY27 (confidence in 30% run-rate); Margin: Protect 11% EBITDA, target 42% Gross Margin in 2-3 years (+1% annually); Order Inflow: Induction demand > capacity; Capex: ~INR 40 Cr for FY27 (maintenance & minor lines), major cycle complete.
order book & pipeline: Demand for induction cooktops exceeds current 4-5 Mn unit annualized capacity; IKEA pipeline valued at INR 200-250 Cr at full capacity (3 lines phasing in through FY27); Export orders normalizing post-tariff reduction.
segment / subsidiary detail: Induction Cooktops: 15.5% of revenue, +89.4% value growth, +67.3% volume growth; Small Appliances: 40.2% of revenue, +12.7% value growth, +97.7% volume growth (mix shift to lower ASP items); Cookware: Strong premiumization from aluminum to stainless steel; HoReCa: New 3,500W infrared launch.
growth verticals / optionality: IKEA global sourcing (INR 200-250 Cr potential); US export market reopening (tariff drop to 18%); Retail store network scaling to 500 by 2027 (currently 329); Capacity utilization upside beyond 5 Mn units.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin stable at 38.6% despite commodity inflation (Aluminum/Steel) due to 10% price hikes passed in Q4; EBITDA margin expanded 113 bps to 9.5%; Opex grew 41% YoY driven by sales commissions (franchise model), freight, and warranty provisions aligned with 32% sales growth.
capex / expansion: FY26 capitalized capex INR 111 Cr (net cash outflow ~INR 70-75 Cr after supplier credit); Major cycle complete; FY27 guidance ~INR 40 Cr for retail expansion and minor assembly line tweaks; IKEA plant fully capitalized as of Mar '26.
capital allocation: Debt repayment prioritized; Shift to Franchise-Owned/Franchise-Operated (FOFO) and Company-Owned/Franchise-Operated (COFO) models to reduce capital intensity of retail expansion; Inventory stocking (45-60 days) for raw materials to hedge against metal price inflation.
risks & watch-items: Forex volatility (significant loss in Q4); Raw material price inflation (Aluminum, Steel, Glass); Supply chain dependency on Chinese components (crystalline glass, magnets); Competition in e-commerce channel; Execution risk on rapid retail franchise rollout.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on volume growth (>15% guidance); Pragmatic on margins (protecting 11% EBITDA while absorbing forex hits); Transparent on accounting distortions (lease liability, supplier credit); Focused on market share leadership in induction.
non-obvious takeaways: Retail store average sales increased from INR 3.8L to INR 4.7L, with breakeven at INR 2.5L, making new stores immediately accretive; Right-of-Use assets dropped from INR 160 Cr to INR 62 Cr due to accounting change (useful life reduced from 9 to 3 years), artificially depressing assets/liabilities; 97.7% volume growth in small appliances vs 12.7% value growth indicates a strategic mix shift to high-volume, lower-ASP entry-level products to capture market share.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Surge in demand for energy-efficient cooking due to geopolitical instability and LPG constraints | Stove Kraft Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of Iran war-induced induction surge and US tariff reductions; backward integration shields against supply chain shocks. |
| Rising aluminum and steel prices compressing margins for non-integrated players | Competitors lacking backward integration | loser | Med | Stove Kraft's ability to pass on 10% price hikes and hedge raw materials puts pressure on assemblers with imported PCBs/components. |

themes.title: Consumer durables, cooling & electricals
themes.need: Rising incomes, electrification and a record cooling season drive consumer-electricals and appliances - HAVELLS/VOLTAS/BLUESTARCO/SYMPHONY/ORIENTELEC on cooling & electricals; TTKPRESTIG/STOVEKRAFT/BAJAJELEC/EUREKAFORB on kitchen/home; CROMPTON-tier fans & pumps; premiumization + GST 2.0 + summer demand expand the organized share. Q1FY27's small-cap read: SONAMLTD grew revenue 75.6% YoY to INR 66.57cr on a cheap raw-material inventory position taken 6-7 months in advance while selling prices rose - management explicitly called the 75% print non-repeatable and guided FY27 to 25-30% with a Q2 floor of INR 40-50cr - and is pivoting from volume to INR 5,000-15,000 value clocks with capacity utilisation still only 60-70%.
themes.driver: Summer cooling demand; GST 2.0 price cuts; festive restocking; commodity-cost tailwind on margins; premiumization/ASP mix shift.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Multi-brand approach to capture the entire value chain": Pigeon at the Value tier, described as a "20+ year old brand" and "one of the market leaders for certain products such as cookware" (sourced to an F&S Report), and Gilma at the Semi-Premium tier.
- Gilma is a distinct route to market, not just a label — "launched in 2016 and manufacturing commenced in 2019", it "offers a modular kitchen experience", "comprises chimneys, hobs and cooktops across price ranges and designs", and is "sold exclusively through Gilma branded outlets, which are owned and operated by franchisees", with a Gilma-specific mobile app for post-sales service requests.
- Brand-wise sales show the Pigeon-led concentration widening: the Pigeon series runs 226.8 → 235.4 → 270.1 → 403.4 (INR Cr, Q1 FY24 → Q1 FY27), OEM 38.8 → 58.3 → 65.7 → 73.3, and "Others*" shrinking 26.4 → 14.6 → 4.4 → 3.2.
- Gross-margin expansion is attributed to brand strength rather than price: margins expanded "despite ongoing supply chain challenges and elevated raw material costs, underscoring the company's healthy brand recall and operational excellence".
- Product breadth spans cookware (pressure cooker, wonder cast, non-stick, electric rice cookers, titanium hard anodized), cooktops and kitchen solutions (hobs, glass/stainless steel/induction cooktops, chimneys), small appliances (mixer grinders, blenders, kettles, toasters, air fryers, electric grills and more) and other products (emergency lamps, flasks, vacuum cleaners, BLDC fan, personal grooming), alongside LED bulbs, battens, downlights, kitchen sinks and water heaters.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [IKEA partnership] The milestones slide records the company having "entered into a strategic partnership with IKEA to develop cookware products" (the extract's year labels are unbound, so the date is not asserted here).
- [Demand shock] The induction upcycle is explicitly tied to an external event: "With the sudden dearth of LPG gas cylinders, the country saw a sudden spike in the purchase of induction cooktops", and the ICT commentary references "pre-war levels" — a demand driver outside management's control.
- [Working capital contradiction] The deck gives two different readings of the same 45-day figure: highlight 05 says "net working capital increased to 45 days from 23 days in Q4FY26, reflecting a strategic inventory build-up ahead of the festive season", while the working-capital note says "despite festive season inventory build-up, inventory days improved to 45 from 69 in Q1FY26". Separately the working-capital bar chart shows inventory days of 158, receivable days 28 and payable days 140 for Q1FY27 (FY25: 144/33/113; FY26: 133/26/136). Both readings are recorded as printed; no reconciliation is attempted.
- [Marketing scale] The "Ex Ko Karo Exchange" campaign reviving the Pigeon exchange offer reported 43.5 million reach, 6.3 million YouTube views, 1.27 million clicks and 30k+ high-intent leads, supported by national print ads, PR in national and vernacular publications, influencer/vox-pop content and point-of-sale branding.
- [Board addition] Mr. Chandru Kalro, former Managing Director of TTK Prestige Limited, sits on the board as Non-Executive Independent Director, bringing "over 35 years of leadership experience in the consumer durables industry" — a direct competitor pedigree on the board.
